DATED: 01/07/2022  IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  R/CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION NO. 10834 of 2022 ==========================================================
 SANJAYBHAI CHUNILAL AASHRA  Versus  STATE OF GUJARAT ==========================================================
Appearance:
MR PM DAVE(263) for the Applicant(s) No. 1,2,3 VISHAL K ANANDJIWALA(7798) for the Applicant(s) No. 1,2,3 MS KRINA CALA, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1 ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE ILESH J. VORA  Date : 01/07/2022  ORAL ORDER 1.

sentences.text: This application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 is for grant of regular bail to the applicants in connection with the FIR being C.R.No. 11189001220246 of 2022 registered at Halvad Police Station, Morbi, for the offence punishable under Sections 304, 308, 114 of IPC and Section 3A and 14 of the Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition & Regulation) Act, 1986.

entities.text: Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition & Regulation) Act, 1986
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
2. Heard learned Senior Counsel Mr. K.B.Anandjiwala assisted by Mr. P.M.Dave, learned counsel for the applicants and learned APP Ms. Krina Calla, for the State.
3. Mr. Anandjiwala, learned Senior Counsel for the applicants urged the following contentions:-
(I) The applicants have not committed any offence as alleged in the FIR and there is no prima facie evidence, involving the applicants in the alleged offence.
(ii) The applicants have been wrongly implicated in the offence.

Reiterating the facts of the FIR, it was submitted that, due to collapsed of factory wall, 12 persons lost their lives, R/CR.MA/10834/2022 ORDER DATED: 01/07/2022 which is unfortunate incident, however, facts remain that, the applicants were employed for Sanjaybhai Chunilal Aashra vs State Of Gujarat on 1 July, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163462458/
1

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: doing supervisory work and before their recruitment, the construction of shed as well as partition wall was being constructed by the owner of the company.

In such circumstances, the applicants having no knowledge about the quality of construction and therefore, no inference can be raised with respect to negligence and as such there is no direct nexus between the applicants and death of the victims.
(iii) It was submitted that, the applicants are charged with Sections 304 of IPC.
Section 304 provides for punishment of culpable homicide not amounting to murder.

Bare reading of Section, there are two kind of punishments applying to two different circumstances; (1) if the act by which death is caused is done with intention of causing death or such bodily injury as is likely to cause death, and (2) if the act is done with knowledge i.e. likely to cause death, but without any intention to cause death.

In this context, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, it was submitted that, the applicants being employees cannot held liable for the unfortunate incident as the factory was constructed in the year 2012 and thereafter, the applicants were recruited for doing supervisory work.
The factory is established for production of refined iodized salt, with the necessary approval from the competent authority and also got license from Food Safety and Standards Authority of India.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
4. In the aforesaid contentions, learned Senior Counsel submitted that the applicants are in custody since 20.05.2022 and investigation is virtually over and as such they do not have any criminal record and are easily available at the time of trial and therefore, discretion may kindly be exercised in favour of the applicants by enlarging them on bail.
R/CR.MA/10834/2022 ORDER DATED: 01/07/2022 5.
Opposing the bail application, learned APP Mrs. Krina Calla, contended that in the alleged mishap, 12 persons lost their lives.

The applicants being responsible persons of the factory,
permitted the labourers to store huge quantity of manufactured salt bags adjacent to the wall, which led to unfortunate incident.

Thus, therefore, learned APP submitted that, looking to the facts of the case and the manner in which, the applicants permitted the labourers to store the huge quantity of salt bags, element of intention can be attributed to the present applicants and therefore, prima facie,
it is established that death of 12 persons caused by act of the applicants and they knew that such act is likely to cause death.
6. Heard at length the counsel for the respective parties and perused the material placed on record.
7.
In order to appreciate the rival submissions, following facts of the case are required to be recorded:-

The alleged incident took place on 18.05.2022 at about 12 AM at village Halvad, Dist.
Morbi.
The 12 persons who have lost their lives were labourers, worked with Sagar Chem Food Industries, having its manufacturing process at GIDC, Halvad.
The company is engaged in the business of salt, spices etc.

As per the prosecution case,
Sanjaybhai Chunilal Aashra vs State Of Gujarat on 1 July, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163462458/

sentences.text: the partition wall of the factory shed admeasuring 100 x 12 sq.ft., suddenly collapsed on the manufacturing site where the workers were engaged in manufacturing process, as a result of which, 12 persons suffered fatal injuries and succumbed to the injures and some of the persons sustained grievous injuries.
Initially, accidental death was registered.
During the investigation, it revealed that, 700 bags of ready salt were stored adjacent to the wall, using as retaining wall and due to heavy load, the wall R/CR.MA/10834/2022 ORDER DATED: 01/07/2022
suddenly collapsed.
The experts from the office of R & B and GERI took visit at the place and taken necessary samples for forensic analysis.
One of the labourer lodged an FIR for the alleged offences as referred above.
It was found that the owner of the factory failed to obtain structural stability certificate from the competent authority as contemplated under the applicable laws and rules thereunder.
In the aforementioned facts, FIR against 8 persons was lodged, who are owner and day to day in-charge of the company.
The applicants have been arrested as accused No.4, 6 & 7 as they are working as supervisor in the company.

8. Having considered the facts and circumstances of the present case, this is a case where the applicants need to be enlarged on bail for the following reasons:-
(I) The construction of the factory completed in the year 2012 for which necessary permission was granted by the local authority.
The applicants have been employed after completion of the construction.
Nothing brought on record to suggest that, the applicants were knew that the partition wall constructed without obtaining structural stability certificate.

(ii) The accused Nos.1 to 3 who are owner and in-charge of day to day operation of the factory having all knowledge about the construction of the partition wall,
investigating agency is not so much sensitive and serious to interrogate them and still they are not arrested.

(iii) Considering the nature of job of the applicants and day to day performance of their duty, it cannot be inferred that they had intention and knowledge that, the partition wall would collapse, which may likely to cause death.

In view of the foregoing reason, so far applicants are R/CR.MA/10834/2022 ORDER DATED:
01/07/2022 concerned, investigation is virtually over.
They are in custody since 20.05.2022 and when they do not have any past criminal record and are easily available at the time of trial, keeping them behind bar would not serve fruitful purpose.
Thus, therefore, without discussing anything on merits of the case I inclined to release the applicants on bail.

sentences.text: If breach of any of the above conditions is committed, the Sessions Judge concerned will be free to issue warrant or take appropriate action in the matter.
Bail bond to be executed before the learned Lower Court having jurisdiction to try the case.
It will be open for the concerned Court to delete, modify and/or relax any of the above conditions, in accordance with law.

At the trial, learned Trial Court shall not be influenced by the observations of preliminary nature,
qua the evidence at this stage, made by this Court while enlarging the applicants on bail.
Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent.
Direct service is permitted.

(ILESH J. VORA,J) SUCHIT Sanjaybhai Chunilal Aashra vs State Of Gujarat on 1 July, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163462458/
